title: hosting.com review (2027): shared plans, Black Friday first-term prices and renewal rates (formerly A2 Hosting) | ScaleHostReview
headings: What the shared cards list, as published
What are the pros and cons, from the published pages?
Who is it for, and who should skip it?
text: hosting.com Visit hosting.com May earn a commission. hosting.com is the current name of the company previously known as A2 Hosting. Its official A2 Hosting comparison page and a customer-review block on the renewal-pricing page both describe the business as formerly A2 Hosting, or previously A2 Hosting. This review summarises the homepage , the web hosting page , the Black Friday 2026 deals page and the Hosting for WordPress page , all read on 14 November 2026, together with the official US-dollar plan catalog that those shared-hosting cards load on the same day. We did not host a site on hosting.com, measure its speed or score it on our rubric, so there is no editorial score on this page. hosting.com's official wordmark, shown to identify the brand. Short answer: the shared web hosting cards on the homepage and hosting page are Starter, Pro and Max. On 14 November 2026, during a Black Friday promotion, the official catalog behind those cards priced a 12-month Starter term at $1.49 a month ($17.88 for the first year), Pro at $3.49 a month ($41.88) and Max at $5.99 a month ($71.88). The same catalog's regular rates, which also appear as the month-to-month prices, are $13.99, $19.99 and $27.99 a month. Starter lists 5 websites and 15GB of NVMe storage; Pro lists 10 websites and 50GB; Max lists 50 websites and 100GB. The same pages advertise a 30-day money-back guarantee, 24/7 support, free managed migration, a free domain for the first year, free SSL and daily backups. The Black Friday page says those intro prices are for the first 12 months and that the plan then renews at the regular price shown before you pay. Promotional first-term rates change, so recheck the live card, including the regular or renewal amount, before you pay. For a managed cloud server you size yourself, see Cloudways vs DigitalOcean . For WordPress-only managed hosting, see the Rocket.net review or the WPX review . Shared plan prices (read 14 November 2026) The homepage headline on 14 November 2026 was "Up to 89% off this Black Friday," with web hosting "from $1.49/mo." The Black Friday page says the deal is on 12-month plans, that you pay the Black Friday price for the first 12 months, and that the plan then "renews at the regular price, which we show you before you pay." The dollar amounts on the Starter, Pro and Max cards themselves are loaded from hosting.com's official plan catalog rather than being printed as static text in the page HTML. The 12-month first-term amounts, the matching first-term totals, and the regular monthly amounts in that catalog, in US dollars, were: Shared plan 12-month first-term monthly amount (Black Friday promo) First-term total billed for 12 months Regular monthly amount (month-to-month, and the 12-month list price before the promo) Websites listed on the shared cards Storage listed on the shared cards Starter $1.49/mo $17.88 $13.99/mo ($167.88 for 12 months at the regular rate) 5 15GB NVMe Pro $3.49/mo $41.88 $19.99/mo ($239.88 for 12 months at the regular rate) 10 50GB NVMe Max $5.99/mo $71.88 $27.99/mo ($335.88 for 12 months at the regular rate) 50 100GB NVMe Sources: the homepage for the $1.49/mo headline and the Starter, Pro and Max feature lists; the Black Friday 2026 page for the 12-month first-term structure, the statement that the plan renews at the regular price shown before you pay, and the 30-day money-back guarantee; and the official US-dollar plan catalog that those cards load, read 14 November 2026, for the dollar amounts, first-term totals and regular rates. The regular 12-month list totals ($167.88, $239.88 and $335.88) equal 12 times the month-to-month rates. The catalog attaches an auto-applied Black Friday promotion named "[BF2026] Black Friday - Web Hosting" to the prepaid terms for new customers. We did not complete a checkout, so confirm the live card and the amount due at payment. The same catalog also lists other prepaid terms. Month-to-month Starter, Pro and Max had no promotional discount in that reading, so they start at the regular rates. The promotional monthly amounts on the longer prepaid terms were: Shared plan Month-to-month 12-month promo monthly amount 24-month promo monthly amount 36-month promo monthly amount 48-month promo monthly amount Starter $13.99/mo $1.49/mo $2.49/mo $2.49/mo $1.99/mo Pro $19.99/mo $3.49/mo $3.99/mo $3.99/mo $3.49/mo Max $27.99/mo $5.99/mo $7.49/mo $7.49/mo $6.99/mo Source: the same official US-dollar plan catalog, read 14 November 2026. These are catalog monthly amounts, not a separate "renews at" line printed on a static page. The Black Friday FAQ is the public page that says the promotional price applies to the first 12 months and that renewal is at the regular price. The catalog product descriptions also say "All discounts apply for the first billing term only." Two official pages disagree about how long the Black Friday offer runs. The Black Friday FAQ says deals start on 2 November 2026 and run until 14 December 2026, with the same prices through Cyber Monday on 30 November. The catalog promotion's short description says the coupon replaces other web hosting promos "from 01-11-26 to and incl. 01-12-26." We are reporting both dates rather than picking one. Recheck the live offer before you pay. Plans and prices change. Check current pricing on the official page: hosting.com/black-friday/ . First-term 12-month promotional monthly amounts against the regular monthly rates in the official catalog. Diagram drawn by the editorial team from the figures in this article. What the shared cards list, as published The homepage and web hosting page list the following on the shared Starter, Pro and Max cards, read 14 November 2026: Starter: 5 websites, an AI website builder for WordPress, email and security included, 15GB NVMe disk space, free domain name registration, malware detection and removal, free managed migration, a free SSL certificate, daily backups, and an OpenAPI and MCP server Pro: everything on Starter, plus 10 websites, 50GB NVMe disk space, more CPU and RAM, staging sites, preview URLs, a Claude Skills pack, and Node.js support Max: everything on Pro, plus 50 websites, 100GB NVMe storage, the highest CPU and RAM of the three shared cards, 40 mailboxes, a service level agreement, a premium SSL certificate, and priority support The same pages advertise a 30-day money-back guarantee. The Black Friday FAQ says domain registrations are not refundable, because they are registered in your name straight away; if you cancel within 30 days, hosting.com says it refunds the hosting and you keep the domain. The FAQ also says a free domain for the first year is included on every plan except Mini, and that the domain then renews at the standard price for that extension. We did not buy a plan or open a support ticket, so those are published terms, not tests we performed. The official Starter product listing in the same catalog also describes "3 staging websites." The homepage Starter bullet list we read does not mention staging; staging sites are listed as a Pro extra. We are reporting both. Confirm staging on the specific plan you are about to take. Where other official pages disagree Several official hosting.com pages describe plan names, website caps or intro prices that do not match the shared Starter, Pro and Max cards on the homepage. We are not treating those pages as a substitute for the shared-card catalog above, and we are not inventing a single reconciled table: The A2 Hosting comparison page , read 14 November 2026, compares old A2 plans with a four-plan hosting.com line (Starter, Plus, Pro and Max). Its "now" intro prices are $3.99, $3.99, $6.99 and $8.99 a month on a 1-year term. Those figures do not match either the Black Friday 12-month catalog amounts ($1.49, $3.49 and $5.99) or the regular rates ($13.99, $19.99 and $27.99). That page also lists a Plus plan, gives Max 100 websites rather than 50, and publishes RAM, vCPU and IOPS figures (for example Starter 2GB RAM and 2 vCPU, Pro 6GB RAM and 4 vCPU, Max 8GB RAM and 4 vCPU). The shared homepage cards do not print those resource numbers, and they do not mention a Plus plan. The published website caps are not consistent across official product lines: the shared cards list 5, 10 and 50 websites, while the A2 comparison page lists 1, 2, 10 and 100 websites on Starter, Plus, Pro and Max. The renewal-pricing page explains that promotional prepaid terms later renew at regular pricing, and that those regular rates are shown before checkout, but it does not print a plan-by-plan renewal table. If you need a figure that only appears on one of those other pages, confirm it on the live checkout for the exact product you are buying. Managed cloud servers, in brief The homepage and hosting page also have a "your own server" tab, described as a cloud server, sometimes called a VPS, with dedicated resources. The four cards we read were labelled 4GB, 8GB, 16GB and 32GB Cloud Server. The official catalog for those products, read 14 November 2026, listed: Managed cloud server (homepage tab) Memory / CPU / storage listed on the homepage cards Month-to-month 12-, 24- or 36-month monthly amount 4GB Cloud Server 4GB memory, 2 CPU cores, 100GB NVMe $48/mo $40/mo 8GB Cloud Server 8GB memory, 4 CPU cores, 150GB NVMe $59/mo $50/mo 16GB Cloud Server 16GB memory, 8 CPU cores, 300GB NVMe $119/mo $100/mo 32GB Cloud Server 32GB memory, 16 CPU cores, 400GB NVMe $239/mo $200/mo Sources: the homepage and web hosting page for the card names and the memory, CPU and storage bullets, and the official US-dollar catalog those cards load, read 14 November 2026, for the dollar amounts. The 12-, 24- and 36-month terms in that catalog used the same monthly amount on each plan ($40, $50, $100 and $200). We did not see a promotional discount on those cloud-server terms in that reading. Recheck the live cards if a VPS is what you need. What are the pros and cons, from the published pages? Pros ✓ During the Black Friday 12-month promo, first-term Starter, Pro and Max amounts are low compared with the regular rates, if a prepaid year works for you ✓ The regular monthly rates are in the same official catalog as the promo amounts, and the Black Friday page says renewal is at the regular price shown before you pay ✓ A 30-day money-back guarantee is advertised, with the FAQ caveat that domain registrations are not refundable ✓ Shared cards list free managed migration, a first-year domain (except Mini), free SSL, daily backups, email and 24/7 support ✓ You can start on shared hosting and, on the same site, look at a managed cloud server if you later want dedicated resources Cons ✕ The regular rate is much higher than the 12-month Black Friday intro: Starter goes from $1.49 to $13.99 a month ✕ The promotional first-term prices are time-limited; official pages disagree on whether the offer ends on 1 December or 14 December 2026 ✕ These shared cards are not a managed cloud server you size yourself, and they are not a WordPress-only managed host of the Rocket.net or WPX type ✕ Official pages disagree on website caps, whether a Plus plan exists, and the intro prices, so you have to confirm the live checkout ✕ We have not hosted a site or measured speed, so we do not score hosting.com or confirm performance or support claims Who is it for, and who should skip it? Good fit ✓ A first WordPress or small-business site, if the 12-month prepaid term and the regular rate after that both work for you ✓ Someone comparing budget shared hosts: start with our cheap hosting guide , and check first-term and regular prices on every card ✓ Someone who may later want a managed cloud server from the same company, and has read the cloud-server catalog amounts above Look elsewhere if ✕ You want a managed cloud server you can resize by the month from a host we already score: see Cloudways, or DigitalOcean if you will run the server yourself ✕ You want WordPress-only managed hosting with unmetered visits listed on the plan card: see the Rocket.net or WPX reviews ✕ You want a scored, side-by-side pick from our existing hosting rubric: start with our best managed WordPress hosting guide What are the alternatives? The regular rates in the same catalog, which also appear as the month-to-month prices, are $13.99, $19.99 and $27.99 a month. title: Hosting.com Review 2026: Plan Prices, Renewal Costs, and Buyer Fit | HostDecider
headings: Hosting.com shared hosting prices on October 5, 2026
The renewal math, refunds, and billing details
The A2 Hosting transition: what carried over
text: Method Desk research Checked Oct 5, 2026 Sources 11 Limits: No paid account was used: we did not purchase a Hosting.com plan or run speed, uptime, migration, or support tests; performance figures come from the cited third-party tests. Dollar figures, promotional discounts, and per-term rates were read on October 5, 2026 from Hosting.com's own live pricing widgets and the checkout price configuration they render (captured in the pricing evidence dossier in this repository); promotions apply to the first billing term only and can change without notice, and checkout totals exclude taxes and add-ons. Independent sources published between June and October 2026 describe different plan lineups, prices, data center lists, and uptime figures; where they conflict, this review defers to the current official pages. The rebrand from A2 Hosting is recent, so long-term reliability under the new ownership could not be verified from desk research. Editorial verdict +/- Conditional medium confidence Hosting.com pairs low first-term prices with a fast LiteSpeed stack, six data center regions, and a complete included bundle, but renewals run roughly two to three times the intro rate, the refund window is now a standard 30 days, and the ownership transition is recent enough to price in. A strong buy on the first term with eyes open, conditional beyond it. Best for First-term buyers who want LiteSpeed speed with a free domain, SSL, daily backups, and free migration included A2 Hosting customers checking the successor brand, since cPanel and the old network are still in service Sites with audiences outside the US that benefit from six data center regions Small portfolios of 5 to 50 sites on one plan, or WordPress users who want a Rocket.net-backed managed tier Avoid if You need predictable renewal pricing rather than a steep jump after the first term You want a refund window longer than 30 days, or need VPS and dedicated servers covered by the guarantee You want a provider with a settled multi-year track record under its current brand Your site needs more than 30 concurrent visitors or 200,000 inodes on the entry plan On this page Hosting.com is the new name of A2 Hosting, the speed-focused host that started in Ann Arbor, Michigan in 2001 and now operates under World Host Group, which acquired the company in January 2025 and rebranded it in late April 2025. [S6] [S7] [S11] Every a2hosting.com address redirects to hosting.com, the shared plans are now called Starter, Pro, and Max, and customers log in at my.hosting.com. [S11] The rebrand changed more than the name. The plan lineup, the refund window, and the managed WordPress platform are all different from the A2 era, and current promotions are aggressive: shared plans are advertised from $1.99 per month on a 48-month prepay. [S2] [S6] [S11] This review answers the buyer question underneath the marketing: what you actually pay across terms, what happens at renewal, what each plan really includes, and whether the transition year should change your decision. The short version: the first-term prices are among the strongest in LiteSpeed shared hosting with a six-region network, the renewal rates are where the math changes, and the ownership change is recent enough to be a real factor. [S2] [S3] [S6] [S7] Bottom line Verdict: conditional. Hosting.com’s shared plans combine low first-term prices with a complete bundle: a free domain for the first year, free SSL, daily backups with 30-day retention, free managed migration, malware detection and removal, DDoS protection, five mailboxes on the base plan, and OpenAPI plus an MCP server on every tier. [S2] [S3] Independent testing is positive on performance: WebHostingCat measured an average 367 ms response time under 250 concurrent users with zero errors and gave the service a 93% overall score, and HostGage rates it 4.0 out of 5 while calling the speed pedigree genuine. [S6] [S9] The conditions: first-term discounts renew at roughly two to three times the intro rate, the money-back window is now a standard 30 days rather than the longer guarantee A2 once advertised, independent trackers still describe an outdated four-plan lineup, and reviewers report rough edges from the transition. [S6] [S7] [S8] This is a desk-research review built from Hosting.com’s official pages and independent reviews published in 2026. We did not purchase a plan or run speed, uptime, migration, or support tests. Hosting.com shared hosting prices on October 5, 2026 Hosting.com sells three shared plans, and the deeper you prepay, the lower the promotional rate: the advertised $1.99 per month on Starter requires a 48-month term. [S2] The table below shows the full ladder as captured from Hosting.com’s live pricing systems on October 5, 2026. Plan Monthly 1 year 2 years 3 years 4 years Regular rate Starter (5 sites) $13.99/mo $2.99/mo ($35.88) $2.79/mo ($66.95) $2.49/mo ($89.65) $1.99/mo ($95.49) $13.99/mo Pro (10 sites) $19.99/mo $4.99/mo ($59.87) $4.79/mo ($114.95) $3.99/mo ($143.64) $3.79/mo ($181.93) $19.99/mo Max (50 sites) $27.99/mo $9.49/mo ($113.86) $8.94/mo ($214.56) $7.99/mo ($287.68) $7.79/mo ($373.90) $27.99/mo Figures are per month with the first-term total in brackets. The checkout is explicit that “all discounts apply for the first billing term only,” so the regular rate column is what a renewal is based on. [S2] Renewal pricing can depend on the term you choose at renewal: Shellz captured a Starter example where the first year cost $35.88 and the following 12 months were billed at $143.88, an increase of 301%. [S7] Two checkout details matter for budgeting. Subscriptions renew automatically unless cancelled, and a saved payment method may be charged three days before the renewal date; promotional prices are for new orders. [S7] Promotions can also differ by page, region, product, and term, so the number in your cart is the one to trust. [S7] What each shared plan includes The differences between tiers are mostly resource limits, not features. [S3] Limit Starter Pro Max Websites 5 10 50 NVMe storage 15 GB 50 GB 100 GB Monthly page view capacity 50,000 150,000 500,000 File count limit (inodes) 200,000 400,000 1 million Concurrent visitor capacity 30 60 120 RAM 2 GB 4 GB 8 GB CPU cores 2 (virtual) 4 (virtual) 4 (virtual) Mailboxes 5 20 40 I/O bandwidth 50 MB/s 100 MB/s 250 MB/s Staging sites Not included Included Included Every tier also includes a free .com, .org, or .net domain for the first year, free SSL, LiteSpeed caching with tuned MySQL, daily backups with 30-day retention and self-serve restore, free managed migration with no per-move fees, malware detection and removal, DDoS protection, an AI website builder for WordPress, one-click site cloning, and API plus MCP support. [S1] [S2] [S3] Mailboxes include 10 GB of storage each with a 2,400 per day sending limit. [S3] Pro and Max add staging sites and preview URLs, and Pro adds a “Claude Skills Pack” for agentic workflows; Max adds priority support, a premium SSL certificate, and an AI chatbot for your own site. [S1] [S2] One discrepancy to check at checkout: the plans page and the comparison matrix list staging sites as a Pro-and-up feature, while the Starter checkout description mentions “3 staging websites.” If staging matters to you, confirm which is correct before ordering. [S2] [S3] The renewal math, refunds, and billing details The single most important number for a buyer is not the promo rate but what you pay after it. Both detailed independent reviews put renewals at roughly two to three times the intro price. [S6] [S7] HostGage’s quick reference warns that “renewals run roughly two to three times the intro price,” and Shellz’s captured example shows a Starter plan going from $35.88 for the first 12 months to $143.88 for the next 12, a 301% increase. [S6] [S7] The guarantee changed in the rebrand: Hosting.com’s money-back window is a standard 30 days, covering eligible shared, WordPress, email, and reseller hosting purchased directly. Domains, renewals and transfers, VPS, dedicated servers, SSL certificates, and some third-party products are excluded. [S6] [S7] A2 Hosting used to advertise a longer anytime guarantee, so buyers who remember that should read the current terms fresh. [S6] Hosting.com’s marketing says “no hidden fees, no lock-ins or minimum terms,” which is true about contract length, but the discount structure still makes the renewal rate the number to budget for. [S2] [S7] Performance, infrastructure, and uptime Hosting.com’s platform runs LiteSpeed with tuned MySQL, NVMe storage, and AMD EPYC processors across all shared plans, with caching, load balancing, and high-availability architecture behind them. [S2] [S3] The “Turbo” branding from the A2 era now lives mainly in the managed WordPress tier names; current shared plans no longer offer a Turbo server option, and WebHostingCat notes you need the Managed WordPress plans for that level of tuning. [S6] [S9] Data center choice is a genuine differentiator at this price: the current comparison matrix lists USA, Singapore, London, Sydney, Mumbai, and Frankfurt for shared plans and managed servers, with bare metal available in the USA only. [S3] Uptime commitments differ by product: the comparison matrix lists 99.95% for shared plans and managed servers, and 99.99% for bare metal, with uptime service credits on all of them and a formal SLA from the server tiers up. [S3] Third-party sources still quote 99.9% from earlier captures, one of several details to verify rather than assume. [S10] [S11] The strongest independent performance data comes from WebHostingCat, which load-tested the service at 250 concurrent users: average response time 367 ms, minimum 221 ms, maximum 1,729 ms, a 100% success rate, zero errors, and zero timeouts, results it rated “very good” to “excellent.” Its overall review score was 93%, with speed and performance at 90%. [S9] HostGage calls the speed pedigree “genuine” while noting the transition has produced “rough edges,” including lingering A2 branding in places and account areas that have not been fully updated. [S6] Managed WordPress, powered by Rocket.net Hosting.com’s managed WordPress platform is built on Rocket.net, the premium managed WordPress host, which joined in August 2025. [S5] [S11] The official page describes Cloudflare Enterprise CDN with full-page caching, 275+ global edge locations, WP Rocket and Object Cache Pro built in, dual firewalls (Cloudflare Enterprise and Imunify360), WordPress-specific firewall rules, and a support team that only handles WordPress. [S5] Plan Websites NVMe storage Visitors/mo Regular 36-month term 12-month term WP Small 1 20 GB 30,000 $9.99/mo $3.49/mo $4.49/mo WP Medium 5 50 GB 120,000 $17.99/mo $3.99/mo $4.99/mo WP Advanced 15 100 GB 250,000 $25.99/mo $9.49/mo $10.99/mo WP Turbo 50 200 GB 500,000 $34.99/mo $13.49/mo $14.99/mo Object Cache Pro is included from WP Medium up. [S11] All plans include the 30-day money-back guarantee, a free domain registration, malware protection, and free migrations. [S5] If you are weighing the Rocket.net platform itself against its competitors, compare our Rocket.net review ; buying managed WordPress from Hosting.com is now a Rocket.net-powered alternative. Managed servers and bare metal For sites that outgrow shared hosting, Hosting.com sells fully managed servers with isolated resources, dedicated IP addresses, and a 99.95% uptime commitment backed by an SLA and service credits. [S3] [S4] Configuration Monthly billing Annual terms First-term promo 4 GB RAM, 2 CPU cores, 100 GB disk $48/mo $40/mo $36/mo 8 GB RAM, 4 CPU cores, 150 GB disk $59/mo $50/mo $45/mo 16 GB RAM, 8 CPU cores, 300 GB disk $119/mo $100/mo $90/mo 32 GB RAM, 16 CPU cores, 400 GB disk $239/mo $200/mo $180/mo Server promotions are much smaller than the shared hosting ones: the first-term discount is about 10%, and it applies to the first invoice only. [S3] The servers page confirms the fully managed positioning and a 30-day money-back guarantee, and the comparison matrix shows chat, ticket, and phone support on server plans. [S3] [S4] Managed bare metal goes further: DS1 ($299/mo monthly, $269/mo annual) with an AMD EPYC 4245P, 6 cores and 32 GB RAM; DS2 ($399/$359) with an EPYC 4465P, 12 cores and 64 GB; and DS3 ($599/$549) with an EPYC 4545P, 16 cores and 128 GB. All three carry a 99.99% uptime commitment, an SLA, and account management, and they are available in US data centers only. [S3] Support, security, and migration Support runs 24/7/365 in-house across chat, ticket, and phone, with the Orbi AI assistant as a first line and multilingual coverage; Hosting.com’s own site displays a 4.8 out of 5 rating from 7,180 reviews, which is a vendor-displayed figure rather than an independent one. [S1] [S2] [S3] Independent assessments are more mixed. WebHostingCat reports that live chat connection and response times have improved, while its comment section includes a customer complaining that ticket replies are slow, and its reviewer acknowledged “a drop off in features and value” relative to the A2 era. [S9] HostGage describes support as available around the clock but notes the transition has left some account areas not fully updated. [S6] We did not test response times ourselves. Security basics are included on every plan: free SSL certificates, DDoS protection, malware detection and removal, and daily backups with 30-day retention plus self-serve restores, including individual database and mailbox restores and deleted website recovery. [S2] [S3] The managed WordPress platform adds the dual-firewall setup described above. [S5] Migrations are free and unlimited across plans, with no per-move fee; cPanel sites move by backup and restore, and other platforms are handled manually with zero downtime wherever possible. [S2] That matters for buyers leaving another cPanel host, and Shellz lists cPanel availability and migration help among the reasons the successor brand is worth comparing. [S7] The A2 Hosting transition: what carried over If you are coming from A2 Hosting, the practical changes are these: your customer area is now the Hosting Panel at my.hosting.com; the plans you knew were renamed Starter, Pro, and Max; a cPanel version of each plan is still sold for buyers who want the classic panel, alongside Hosting.com’s own panel at the same prices; and old A2 promo codes no longer apply because discounts are now applied automatically at checkout. [S11] The underlying network is still A2’s: its IP addresses are announced from the same autonomous system, still registered under the A2HOSTING name. [S11] HostGage’s June 2026 review of the transition found “early customer grumbles” and lingering A2 branding in places, and recommends judging the service on your first month of performance while keeping your own off-site backups. [S6] WebHostingCat’s reviewer, a long-time A2 tracker, wrote that the feature and value equation has dropped off versus the A2 era while performance remains strong. [S9] Where third-party numbers disagree Because the transition year saw several lineup and pricing changes, older reviews describe a company that no longer quite exists. ComparEdge’s July 2026 pricing tracker still lists a four-tier lineup (Starter, Plus, Pro, and Max) with renewals from $11.99 to $27.99 per month, and says the base plans have no free domain registration. [S8] The current official pages show three tiers (Starter, Pro, Max), a free domain in the first year, and Starter renewing from $13.99 per month, so treat the older figures as historical. [S2] Other discrepancies worth knowing: uptime is quoted as 99.9% by third-party sources versus 99.95% on the current comparison matrix; data center lists vary between sources (the current official list is USA, Singapore, London, Sydney, Mumbai, and Frankfurt, while older reviews list Dallas, Toronto, Mexico City, Michigan, Phoenix, or Amsterdam); and WebHostingCat’s August 2026 capture still described site caps of 1, 2, 10, and 100 sites versus the current 5, 10, and 50. [S3] [S6] [S9] [S10] [S11] Hosting.com pros and cons Pros Low first-term prices on a LiteSpeed, NVMe, and AMD EPYC stack, with six data center regions to choose from. [S2] [S3] A complete included bundle: free domain for the first year, SSL, daily backups with 30-day retention, free managed migration, malware removal, and API plus MCP support. [S2] [S3] Strong independent performance results: 367 ms average response under 250 concurrent users and a 93% overall score. [S9] A clear upgrade path on one platform, from shared hosting to fully managed servers and bare metal. [S3] [S4] Managed WordPress runs on the Rocket.net platform with Cloudflare Enterprise and Object Cache Pro. [S5] [S11] Cons Renewals run roughly two to three times the intro rate, and the $1.99 headline requires a 48-month prepay. [S2] [S6] [S7] The refund window is a standard 30 days and excludes domains, renewals, VPS, dedicated servers, and more. [S6] [S7] The ownership change and rebrand are recent, with rough edges and mixed customer sentiment reported. [S6] [S9] The entry plan has the tightest resource envelope (30 concurrent visitors, 200,000 inodes), and staging is a Pro-and-up feature per the plans page and matrix. [S3] Third-party sources still disagree on plan lineups, uptime, and data centers; verify the cart numbers before buying. [S8] [S10] [S11] Who should choose Hosting.com Hosting.com fits buyers who want a fast LiteSpeed stack at a low first-term price and will go in with clear eyes about renewal: a first website or small portfolio, WordPress sites that want free migration and staging on Pro, and small agencies that can use the 5 to 50 site allowance. [S2] [S3] The six-region network makes it unusually flexible for a host at this price if your audience is outside the US. [S3] It also fits A2 Hosting customers checking on the successor brand, since cPanel and the old network are still in service and migration is free. [S7] [S11] Who should look elsewhere Skip Hosting.com if predictable long-term pricing matters more than a cheap first term, if you need the longest possible refund window, or if you want a provider with a longer independent track record under its current brand. [S6] [S7] [S9] For alternatives with different models, compare HostGator and Hostinger for budget cPanel hosting, SiteGround for support-led shared hosting, DreamHost or Cloudways if you want different pricing structures, and Rocket.net or Pressable for premium managed WordPress. Our best WordPress hosting roundup covers more options. Final verdict Hosting.com earns a conditional recommendation with medium confidence. The first-term prices are among the best available on a LiteSpeed and NVMe stack with real data center choice, the included bundle removes most add-on costs, and the strongest independent test of the current service came back “very good” to “excellent” with a 93% overall score. [S2] [S3] [S9] The conditions are the steep renewal rates, the shortened 30-day refund window, and the recent ownership transition, which shows up as rough edges and mixed sentiment in independent reviews. [S6] [S7] [S9] The practical decision rule: buy the first term for what it is, price the renewal into your plan from day one, and verify the cart against the official terms on the day you order. text: If you've been around WordPress for a while, you probably know A2 Hosting, the speed-focused host from Ann Arbor, Michigan. Well, A2 Hosting now goes by a new name: Hosting.com. Type a2hosting.com into your browser today and it sends you straight to hosting.com. So, here is our honest Hosting.com review for 2026, written for anyone wondering what changed and whether it's still a good pick. For this review, we went through every shared, WordPress, VPS and dedicated plan on Hosting.com's website on 6 November 2026. Shared hosting starts at $1.49/mo for the first year, and dedicated servers go up to $499/mo . One thing upfront, though. We didn't buy a plan and run our own speed tests for this review, so any speed claim below is Hosting.com's own, and I'll say so each time. I've used WordPress since 2014, and several of my own eCommerce sites run on it, so I've seen plenty of cheap first-year deals turn expensive at renewal. That's exactly what I looked for here. Like every host, Hosting.com has good sides and bad sides. So, let's have a look at them. All prices in this review are in US dollars and exclude tax, as shown on hosting.com in November 2026. Most intro prices need a 1-year term paid upfront (3 years on unmanaged VPS), and a Black Friday sale was running when we checked. Hosting.com at a Glance Best for bloggers, small businesses and agencies who want lots of features in year one and don't mind a bigger renewal bill Starting price $1.49/mo for the first year (Shared Starter, 1-year term) Renews at $13.99/mo (Shared Starter) Hosting types Shared, managed WordPress, managed and unmanaged VPS, dedicated servers, reseller Formerly A2 Hosting, now combined with World Host Group under one brand Free extras Domain registration, SSL , daily backups, malware removal, free migrations; on WordPress plans, WP Rocket and a premium object cache (Object Cache Pro) Uptime promise 99.99% on managed WordPress plans Support 24/7, with an AI chat assistant called Orbi that hands you to the team Money-back guarantee 30 days (domains, setup and migration fees aren't refundable) Our rating 3.9 out of 5 Hosting.com Review: The Goods Hosting.com packs a lot into its plans, and some of it is stuff other hosts charge extra for. Here's what stood out when we went through the pages. WP Rocket and Object Cache Pro Come Free on WordPress Plans This is the one that caught my eye first. Every managed WordPress plan includes WP Rocket, a popular paid caching plugin , and Object Cache Pro with Relay, a premium tool that speeds up database work. On top of that, you get unlimited PHP workers, a Cloudflare Enterprise CDN with more than 275 edge locations, and full-page caching that's switched on for you. Normally you'd pay for WP Rocket yourself, so this is real value. Security Is Switched On From Day One The WordPress plans run two firewalls: Cloudflare Enterprise and Imunify360. Hosting.com says its rules know the WordPress and plugin attacks people actually use, and malware monitoring and cleanup are included. Shared plans also get a web application firewall and malware detection and removal. You don't have to set any of it up. Lots of Sites, Even on the Cheapest Plan Here's a nice surprise. The $1.49 Shared Starter plan lets you host 5 websites, with 15 GB of NVMe storage and email included. Pro goes to 10 sites, and Max goes all the way to 50 sites with 40 mailboxes. On the WordPress side, Medium covers 5 installs and Turbo covers 50. For someone running a few small sites, that's a lot of room. Backups You Can Go Back 30 Days On Shared plans take daily backups and store them off the server, and you can restore to any point in the last 30 days. Managed WordPress plans keep daily backups for 14 days, plus one-click staging, so you can test changes on a copy before they hit your live site. Free Migrations and a "Faster or a Year Free" Promise Moving from another host? Migrations are free on every WordPress plan, and the shared plans include a free managed migration too. Hosting.com also makes a bold promise on its WordPress page: if your site isn't faster after the move, measured by global average time to first byte, it says you get a year free. We haven't tested that ourselves, so read the terms before you count on it. Modern Hardware and AI Extras The shared servers run on AMD EPYC processors with NVMe storage and LiteSpeed caching. Hosting.com also leans hard into AI: there's an AI website builder for WordPress, an OpenAPI and MCP server on shared plans, and even a "Claude Skills Pack" from the Pro plan up. Whether you need any of that depends on you, but it shows the company is keeping up. Hosting.com Review: The Bads Like any other host, Hosting.com has some rough edges. Most of them come down to one thing: the price after year one. The Renewal Prices Jump a Lot This is the big one, and I won't sugarcoat it. Shared Starter costs $1.49 a month in year one, then renews at $13.99. That's more than nine times higher. Pro goes from $3.49 to $19.99, and Max from $5.99 to $27.99. The WordPress plans jump too, though less: Small goes from $4.49 to $9.99, and Medium from $4.99 to $17.99. Hosting.com first-year prices next to its renewal prices, checked 6 November 2026. So, when you compare hosts, look at the renewal price, not the sticker price. Our true cost calculator helps with exactly that. The Low Price Needs a Full Year Upfront The intro prices are for a 1-year term paid upfront, or 3 years on the unmanaged VPS plans. Pay monthly instead, and the WordPress Small plan is $9.99 from day one. The deal is only "cheap" if you prepay. Some Fees Are Never Refunded There's a 30-day money-back guarantee, which is good. But Hosting.com's refund policy says domain registrations, setup fees and migration fees are not refundable in any case. Plans also renew automatically, so set a reminder before your renewal date if you plan to leave. Shared Plans Have Hidden Limits Shared accounts are capped at 600,000 files (inodes) and 35 connections to the server at the same time, according to the terms of service. That's plenty for a normal blog, but a busy store or a site with a huge media library could hit it. A New Brand Can Be Confusing Hosting.com brings A2 Hosting and World Host Group under one name, and it has also bought Rocket.net. That's not a bad thing, but older A2 Hosting guides and screenshots you find online may not match what you see today. When in doubt, trust what's on hosting.com now. Hosting.com Web Hosting Plans One thing I like here is that you can start small and grow without ever switching companies, because Hosting.com has shared hosting, managed WordPress, VPS servers (managed or not) and full dedicated machines. So, let's walk through them. Shared Web Hosting Shared hosting is where most people start. Year one costs just $1.49/mo , and after that you pay $13.99/mo . As the name itself suggests, lots of customers share one server, which is exactly why it's this cheap. For a blog, a portfolio or a local business site, that's usually all you need. Starter ($1.49/mo, renews $13.99): 5 websites on one plan, which I didn't expect at this price, plus 15 GB of NVMe storage, email, a free domain, daily backups and the AI website builder. Pro ($3.49/mo, renews $19.99): doubles you up to 10 websites and 50 GB, and adds more CPU and RAM, staging, preview URLs and Node.js support. Hosting.com calls it the most popular plan. Max ($5.99/mo, renews $27.99): the big one, with 50 websites, 100 GB, 40 mailboxes, a premium SSL, an SLA and priority support. Shared Hosting Plans Comparison Features Starter Pro Max First year $1.49/mo $3.49/mo $5.99/mo Paid upfront $17.88 $41.88 $71.88 Renews at $13.99/mo $19.99/mo $27.99/mo Buy plan ORDER ORDER ORDER Sites and storage Websites 5 10 50 NVMe storage 15 GB 50 GB 100 GB Extras Staging sites No Yes Yes Priority support No No Yes Before you choose, think about year two. Starter is the cheapest today, but at renewal it costs $13.99 a month for 5 sites, while Pro costs $19.99 for 10 sites and staging. Managed WordPress Hosting Prices start at $4.49/mo for the first year and renew from $9.99/mo . These plans are tuned only for WordPress, with WP Rocket, Object Cache Pro, two firewalls and a 99.99% uptime guarantee on every one. Small ($4.49/mo, renews $9.99): 1 WordPress install, about 30,000 visitors a month, 20 GB of storage and 100 GB of bandwidth. Medium ($4.99/mo, renews $17.99): 5 installs, about 120,000 visitors, 50 GB and 300 GB of bandwidth. This is the most popular one. Advanced ($10.99/mo, renews $25.99): 15 installs, about 250,000 visitors, 100 GB and 600 GB of bandwidth. Turbo ($14.99/mo, renews $34.99): 50 installs, about 500,000 visitors, 200 GB and 1.2 TB of bandwidth, for agencies. Honestly, Medium looks like the sweet spot in year one: just 50 cents more than Small for five times the sites. Just remember it renews at $17.99. VPS Hosting Managed VPS plans with cPanel start at $29/mo for the first year (4 GB of RAM, 2 CPU cores, 100 GB of NVMe) and renew at double the price, $58. The most popular is the 16 GB plan at $70, renewing at $140. Bigger servers go up to 256 GB of RAM. Self-managed VPS plans are much cheaper but need a 3-year term for the best price: from $3.49/mo for 2 GB of RAM, 1 core and 40 GB, renewing at $8.99. The 8 GB plan at $9.99 (renews $24.99) is the most popular. You manage the server yourself. Dedicated Servers Dedicated servers start at $199/mo , billed monthly, with an AMD EPYC 4245P (6 cores), 32 GB of DDR5 RAM and NVMe storage. The $299 plan doubles the cores and RAM, and the $499 plan has 16 cores and 128 GB. They're for big stores and high-traffic sites that need a whole machine. Features of Hosting.com Hosting NVMe storage on every plan Free SSL and free domain registration Daily backups Malware detection and removal Free website migrations LiteSpeed caching on shared plans WP Rocket and Object Cache Pro on WordPress plans Cloudflare Enterprise CDN on WordPress plans AI website builder 30-day money-back guarantee Overall Advantages of Hosting.com Very low first-year prices 5 websites even on the cheapest shared plan WP Rocket and Object Cache Pro included on WordPress plans Two firewalls and malware cleanup on WordPress plans 30-day restore points on shared backups Free migrations Modern AMD EPYC and NVMe hardware Plans from shared all the way to dedicated Overall Disadvantages of Hosting.com Renewal prices are much higher, up to 9 times on Starter Best prices need a year (or three) upfront Domain, setup and migration fees are never refunded File and connection limits on shared plans Older A2 Hosting info online can be out of date Hosting.com vs Hostinger vs Bluehost How does Hosting.com's cheapest shared plan compare with two other popular budget hosts we've reviewed? Here's how the numbers from our own reviews and our hosting comparison line up: Hosting.com Starter: $1.49/mo for a 12-month term, then $13.99/mo, with 5 websites. It's the cheapest first year by far, but the renewal stings. Hostinger Premium: $2.49/mo if you commit to 48 months, then $10.99/mo, with 3 websites. Great if you're happy to lock in for four years. Bluehost Starter: $3.99/mo on a 36-month term, then $9.99/mo, with 10 websites. The gentlest renewal of the three, and the most sites. For more detail, read our Hostinger review and our Bluehost review for 2026 . Who Should Choose Hosting.com? I'd pick Hosting.com for a new WordPress site where I wanted WP Rocket and strong security included, and planned to check the price again before renewal. Agencies will like the Turbo WordPress plan with 50 installs and the 50-site Max shared plan. Developers who want a cheap self-managed VPS should look at the 3-year VPS deals. I'd skip it if I wanted a low price that stays low for years, because the renewal jump is steep. Hosting.com FAQs Is Hosting.com the same as A2 Hosting? Yes, it's the same company. A2 Hosting now runs under the Hosting.com name, and if you visit a2hosting.com, you land on hosting.com. The company describes it as bringing World Host Group and A2 Hosting together under one global brand. Does Hosting.com have a money-back guarantee? Yes. Hosting.com promises a 30-day money-back guarantee on its plan pages. Just know that the fine print leaves a few things out: domain registrations, setup fees and migration fees won't come back to you. How much does Hosting.com cost after the first year? Shared plans renew at $13.99, $19.99 and $27.99 a month. Managed WordPress plans renew at $9.99, $17.99, $25.99 and $34.99 a month. Is Hosting.com good for WordPress? Yes, especially the managed WordPress plans, which include WP Rocket, Object Cache Pro, a Cloudflare Enterprise CDN and two firewalls. Just budget for the renewal price. Conclusion: Our Hosting.com Review Verdict Hosting.com is still the same speed-minded A2 Hosting at heart, just with a new name and a lot more under the hood. The WordPress plans are genuinely generous, with WP Rocket, Object Cache Pro, Cloudflare Enterprise and malware cleanup all included, and even the cheapest shared plan hosts 5 sites. If you read our Hostinger review , you'll see Hostinger renews lower on its entry plan, while Hosting.com gives you more in year one. But here's the catch, and it's a big one: the renewal bill is a lot higher. So, think of the first-year price as a trial run, and budget for the real price. Do that, and Hosting.com is a solid choice, especially for WordPress. We think this Hosting.com review helped you understand what you get and what you pay. Are you using Hosting.com (or A2 Hosting), or thinking about it? Don't forget to leave your feedback in the comment area below. Our verdict Hosting.com 3.9 / 5 Feature-packed plans with WP Rocket, Object Cache Pro, Cloudflare Enterprise and malware cleanup on WordPress, and 5 sites even on the cheapest shared plan. Renewal prices jump a lot, and the best prices need a year upfront. text: Hosting.com review: shared, WordPress and VPS hosting from the former A2 Hosting Hosting.com is the new name of A2 Hosting, a US host that sells shared web hosting, managed WordPress hosting, managed cloud servers and unmanaged Linux VPS. Entry prices are low on long terms, but renewals cost several times more. It suits small businesses, bloggers and agencies that want 24/7 human support and free site migration. Start with Hosting.com Get Hosting.com → Is there a Hosting.com coupon or discount? No coupon applies through this page. The site shows its own intro discounts, for example Starter at $1.99/mo instead of $13.99 on a 4-year term. Facts checked on October 29, 2026 Disclosure: this is an affiliate link. If you sign up or buy through it, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. Prices and terms are set by Hosting.com and can change — check them on the official site. · Something out of date? Quick answers Will Hosting.com move my site for free? Yes. The in-house team migrates sites, email and domains free of charge, with no limit on the number of sites. Does Hosting.com have a money-back guarantee? Yes, 30 days for most products, once per customer and only for the first term. Domains, servers and some third-party licences are excluded. How to get started Open Hosting.com through the link on this page and pick a product: shared hosting, hosting for WordPress or a VPS. Choose a plan and a billing term; the lowest monthly prices need a 3- or 4-year prepayment. Create an account at checkout, add a domain (new, transfer or one you already own) and pay. Ask support for the free managed migration if you are moving an existing site. Manage sites, email and billing in the my.hosting.com dashboard; Orbi, the AI assistant, hands you to a human when needed. What Hosting.com offers Hosting.com is run by A2 Hosting, LLC , a Delaware company that traded as A2 Hosting until the rebrand; the old site says it launched in 2003. Today the line-up is: Shared web hosting (Starter, Pro, Max) on AMD EPYC servers with NVMe storage and LiteSpeed caching, email at your domain, daily off-server backups with restore to any point in the last 30 days, a web application firewall and an AI website builder for WordPress. Managed hosting for WordPress , built with Rocket.net: Cloudflare Enterprise CDN, a dual firewall (Cloudflare + Imunify360), staging, and free WP Rocket and Object Cache Pro from the Medium plan up. Managed cloud servers ("your own server"): 4 to 32 GB of dedicated RAM, fully managed. Unmanaged Linux VPS ("Pro"): root access, Ubuntu, Debian, AlmaLinux or cPanel, 10 locations.
